clue.text: Cheat to start puzzle

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat or swindle them
to found something is to start or establish it

explanation.surface: Someone cheats in order to begin solving a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To puzzle someone is to baffle or bewilder them, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Scoundrel in American intelligence finds bug

indicators.note: the scoundrel is in, so inside, the agency

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a cad is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rogue within the CIA discovers a listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests a spy's microphone; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is a chirping insect, and insects are loosely called bugs.

clue.text: Cloud and rain, finally — I'm taking public transport

indicators.note: finally points to the end letter of rain

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: It's cloudy and finally raining, so I'm catching the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a rain-bearing cloud.

clue.text: Four, five, all regularly seen in college

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: Four or five, all regularly attending college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes O, R, I, E, L from FOURFIVEALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Compound tax for dummies?

indicators.note: the tax is one charged for the dummies, so they come first as in a compound noun

parts.note: a nit is a fool or dummy
a rate is a local tax

explanation.surface: A reference guide titled like 'Tax for Dummies'.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a 'nit rate', a levy for fools. The question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a chemical compound, a salt of nitric acid.

clue.text: Player is wearing tight boot

indicators.note: the anagrammed boot wears, so surrounds, the word is
tight is slang for drunk, so the letters of boot reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer or similar is wearing a boot that pinches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' is slang for drunk, an anagram signal, so it scrambles BOOT to OBOT before 'wearing' wraps it round IS. 'Player' is a musician, not a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe player is a musician, a player in an orchestra.

clue.text: Rabbit led astray where food is put out

indicators.note: astray means gone wrong, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A rabbit wanders off toward where food has been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges RABBITLED.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird table is a garden platform on which food is set for wild birds.

clue.text: Not really a problem one can sleep on?

definitions.text: Not really a problem one can sleep on?

parts.words: Not really a problem one can sleep on?
parts.note: sleeping on a problem means leaving it till morning; this problem is one that stops you sleeping at all

explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is the inability to sleep, a problem that keeps you awake.

clue.text: Adolescent ate green bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A youngster ate unripe bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges ATEGREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person aged thirteen to nineteen, an adolescent.

clue.text: Inherit clubs with mixed emotion

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: mixed signals that the letters of emotion are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone inherits a golf bag or card suit while feeling conflicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges EMOTION into OMEINTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into money is the idiom for receiving a legacy.

clue.text: Take shells from water, anxious, and see fish

indicators.note: a word's shell is its outside, so the first and last letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: An anxious beachcomber collects shells from the water and spots a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take shells from' picks WR, AS and SE from water, anxious and see.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrasse is a family of brightly coloured sea fish.

clue.text: Love but no husband for this regretful lady

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: no means the husband is left out of the word this

explanation.surface: A woman regrets her love life, being left with no husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cole Porter song 'Miss Otis Regrets' is about a lady who cannot lunch today.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Otis in Cole Porter's song sends her regrets, so she is the regretful lady.

clue.text: Bill in close-fitting jacket for performance

indicators.note: the bill sits in, so inside, the jacket

parts.note: a doublet was a man's close-fitting jacket of the Renaissance
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A man named Bill wears a snug jacket for his show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is the account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of comedians or entertainers working together is a stage turn, a performance.

clue.text: Floridian city monkey caught?

indicators.note: caught in the sense of heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to monkey with something is to tamper with it

explanation.surface: Was a monkey captured in a city in Florida?
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent TAMPER and TAMPA sound the same. 'monkey' is a verb, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a large port city on the Gulf coast of Florida.

clue.text: Release without charge

definitions.meaning: to let go or liberate, a verb

explanation.surface: A prisoner is let out with no charges brought.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to liberate and costing nothing, two separate senses.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed, protects Maoists

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
guards means protects

explanation.surface: Someone red-faced shields a group of Mao's followers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Guards were young militants of Mao's Cultural Revolution in China.

clue.text: Glorious under the Linden tree?

parts.note: sub- is the Latin prefix for under
the linden is the lime tree

explanation.surface: It is wonderful to lie under a linden tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime is a synonym for glorious, inspiring awe.

clue.text: Mean 50s lout shut away

parts.note: mean in the stingy sense is close, tight with money
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress, often thought a lout

explanation.surface: A nasty 1950s yob is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective for the lout; it is close (stingy).
explanation.definitionFit: Closeted means kept away in private, shut off from others.

clue.text: Shoot a troublemaker in European city

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant
a pest is a nuisance or troublemaker

explanation.surface: A gunman shoots a hooligan in a continental capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' is the plant growth, not firing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital of Hungary.

clue.text: City subordinate to address filth in lucre?

definitions.note: to clean dirty money, a verb phrase

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
under someone means lower in rank, subordinate to them

explanation.surface: A city official deals with dirty money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filthy lucre' is a phrase for money, so cleaning filth in it means making illicit cash look legitimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundering money passes illegal funds through accounts to hide their source, cleaning dirty money.

clue.text: Climber came up

definitions.meaning: a climbing plant, often trained on trellises
ascended, past tense of to get up or ascend

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a flower that can climb walls and the past tense of arise.

clue.text: Have quick look in either direction

definitions.note: to glance briefly, and the four-letter word for it is a palindrome

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards, so either way gives it

parts.note: to glance briefly, and the four-letter word for it is a palindrome

explanation.surface: A driver glances both ways before crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to take a brief furtive glance.

clue.text: Couple crossing river that is in grassland

indicators.note: the couple crosses, so stretches round, the river

parts.note: a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: Two people cross a stream in open country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts R inside PAIR to make PRAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide treeless grassy plain in North America.

clue.text: Eating too much, mole covered in pimples

indicators.note: the spy eats, so takes inside, the excess

parts.note: a mole is a spy inside an organisation
OTT is over the top, too much

explanation.surface: From overeating, a mole has come out in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' looks like a skin blemish to suit the pimples; it is a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotty describes skin with many spots or pimples.

clue.text: Dragon, mostly green, captured by Welshman

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the Welshman

parts.note: Wyn is a common Welsh man's name

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: A mostly green dragon is caught by a Welshman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims VERT to VER. Fitting, as a red dragon is the Welsh emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a heraldic winged dragon with two legs.

clue.text: United supporters returned in chaos

indicators.note: returned means the pieces are read going back

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names
fans are supporters of a team

explanation.surface: Football fans heading home after a United match cause mayhem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns U + FANS round to read SNAFU.
explanation.definitionFit: Snafu is military slang for a muddled, chaotic situation.

clue.text: Cheerfully irresponsible friends retired in good spirits

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pals are friends
happy means cheerful, in good spirits

explanation.surface: Retired friends are carefree and jolly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns PALS into SLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaphappy describes a casual, carelessly cheerful attitude.

clue.text: Bird over new atomic plant

indicators.note: in a down clue over means above, so the bird comes first

parts.note: a hen is a bird
A is the abbreviation for atomic, as in A-bomb

explanation.surface: A bird flies over a new nuclear power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'atomic plant' suggests a power station; plant is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a shrub whose leaves give a reddish dye.

clue.text: Ambassador blocks Conservative plan

indicators.note: the ambassador blocks the middle of the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A diplomat obstructs a Tory scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: HE = His Excellency, how an ambassador is addressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed scheme or idea, so a plan.

clue.text: Not fair when superior virtually eclipses career

indicators.note: to eclipse is to cover, so the shortened word wraps round the other
virtually means almost, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: better means superior
to career is to run headlong

explanation.surface: It is unjust when a superior overshadows someone's career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' (almost all) trims BETTER to BETTE, which 'eclipses' RUN. 'Not fair' sounds like injustice but refers to hair colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair hair is blond; a brunette has dark hair, so is not fair.

clue.text: Hate exam following low grades

indicators.note: the exam comes after, following the grades

parts.note: D and E are low exam grades
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: A student loathes the exam after getting poor marks.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe intensely.

clue.text: Singer's very nearly changed name

indicators.note: changed signals the letters of nearly are altered in order

explanation.surface: A singer has almost changed her name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns NEARLY into ERALYN. Vera Lynn was the British wartime 'Forces' Sweetheart'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Vera Lynn was a famous British vocalist of the Second World War.
